sutta: 11.9 at savathi monks once in the past a number of seers who were virtuous and a good character has settled down in leaf huts in the trek saka devaraja and vipacity lord of the asuras approached those seers vipacity lord of the asuras put on his boots bound his sword on tightly and with the parasol born aloft enter the hermitage through the main gate then having turned his left side towards them you walk past those seers who were virtuous and a good character asaka devaraja took off his boots handed over his sword to others lowered his parasol his umbrella and entered the hermitage through an ordinary gate or a small game then he stood on the lee side raising his joint hands in reverential salutation being homage to those seers who were virtuous and a good character i stopped here for a moment so you see this saka devaraja and this vipacity sometimes they fight with each other but sometimes they are friends because sakadevaraja has many wives and one of his favorite wise is i think sujan pati and that is the daughter of vaipachitira the lord of the asuras so actually vipacity is the father-in-law of sakadeva so in this utah they went together to see these ascetics in the forest and vipacity wearing his boots and with his sword and his umbrella high up he walked through the main gate quite proudly and with his left side towards them in the left side towards them shows not paying respect because in the indian tradition and probably in the deva tradition if you respect somebody your right side must always face that person but here he turned his left side towards them and walked past them on the other hand asaka devarajah took off his boots our respect and even his sword he handed over to a lesser deva and then lowered his umbrella and entered the hermitage to a small gate then he stood on the lee side on the the lower side of the wind the lower side of the wind so that uh the wind goes first to the ascetics and then to him our respect then monks those seers address sakai in verse the order of the seers long bound by their vows emitted from their bodies goes with the wind turn away from here thousand-eyed god for the seer's odour is foul deva devaraja that the order of the seers long bound by their vows emitted from their bodies go with the wind we yearn for this older available source as for a garland of flowers on the head the devas do not perceive it as repulsive as the end of the sudama so here the seers understood that this was standing up on the lee side in other words when the wind blows the smell of the ascetics the human smell will go to this deva viva rajala so he they know that the human smell is very repulsive but it's very small to the divas and so the asima to not to stand there but he told them that he respect them so much that he he he yearns for the smell just like a garland of flowers on the head  so you see the character of sakadeva is very different from the asura king
